quotes.text: An event doesn't do any work. It carries news and somewhere else, a piece of code reads that news and decides what to do next.

quotes.text: Event grid is a delivery service, not a place where your business logic lives. Its only job is to carry events from the systems that produce them to the systems that consume them.

quotes.text: Dead lettering is the safety net. It's off unless you turn it on, and when you turn it on, you point it at a storage container.

quotes.text: At least once delivery means your handler might see the same event twice, so it's smart to make handlers safe to run more than once.

quotes.text: If you need to send work that must be processed reliably, that's service bus. If you're streaming high volume data to analyze later, that's event hubs. And if you simply need the right code to react when something changes, that's event grid
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

chapters.title: What Azure Event Grid actually is
Event Grid vs. Service Bus vs. Event Hubs

takeaways: Azure Event Grid is a fully managed publish-subscribe service that tells your apps the moment something happens, replacing costly polling with event-driven design.
Events flow from publishers into system, custom or partner topics, and event subscriptions filter them and deliver them to handlers by push or pull.
Event Grid retries failed deliveries and can dead-letter undeliverable events, while Service Bus handles reliable transactional messaging and Event Hubs handles high-volume streaming.
hook: Event Grid, Service Bus and Event Hubs sound alike, and many people stall before they understand which one to use. This Simply Explained episode is for Azure beginners and architects who want a plain-English view of event-driven design, topics, subscriptions, push and pull delivery, retries and dead-lettering, plus a simple rule for choosing the right messaging service.
